Concentration electives
requirements.summary: 200-level or higher with QC code; machine-learning core list and the public elective list are eligible sources. The page conflicts on whether two or all three electives must be COMPSCI. Reuse of a course for multiple requirements is not permitted.

requirements.title: Conditional independent study option
requirements.summary: At most one independent study with substantial AI/ML emphasis in COMPSCI, MATH, STA, ECE, or a related area approved by the DUS may count.

requirements.title: Offering, renumbering and BS eligibility restrictions
requirements.summary: Only STA 332 / MATH 343, not ECE 480, satisfies the BS option. STA 332 was renumbered from STA 432 in Fall 2025; COMPSCI 575 from COMPSCI 572 in Fall 2026. Topics may not be offered regularly; ECON 490 Causality and ML is the Spring 2026 offering. The full elective list is available only in student Stellic.

requirements.title: Concentration declaration
requirements.summary: Use the Academic Plan Change form to add, drop or change the concentration.

requirements.title: Substitutions require review
requirements.summary: Eligibility depends on the academic plan. Consult the DUS and receive approval before counting a substitution; see the department substitution guide.

requirements.title: Catalog applicability and host degree context
requirements.summary: The revised curriculum applies to Fall 2026 first-year matriculants. Earlier matriculants retain prior requirements. The source separately requires 34 units for the BS; host college and general-education requirements are not fully mapped here.

requirements.title: Substitution approval and counting
requirements.summary: Request DUS approval for a substitution, then ask for the record amendment when taking the approved course. A substitution course may satisfy only one requirement; online courses cannot substitute.

requirements.title: Core substitution limitations
requirements.summary: COMPSCI 201 has no substitute. Pratt ECE students need COMPSCI 250D / ECE 250D; other Pratt students should consult their DUS. Courses replacing COMPSCI 230 cannot count elsewhere in the CS major, and substitutes other than 231D/232 require a prerequisite permission request. Conditional two-course combinations are recorded separately under the substitutions-guide note and require DUS approval.

requirements.title: Unresolved substitution scope
requirements.summary: The guide labels the AI mathematics requirement COMPSCI 270L and includes MATH 222, while the current concentration page uses 270 and omits 222. The general elective guide describes an older five-elective structure. Do not apply those alternatives automatically to the current three-elective concentration.

requirements.title: D grades and credential requirements
requirements.summary: The bulletin treats D as a low pass that can satisfy other requirements, while limiting D-graded courses to two toward continuation and the 34-course-credit host degree total. This is a general policy, not an invented minimum AI-course grade.

requirements.title: S/U grading for program requirements
requirements.summary: A voluntarily S/U-graded course cannot satisfy major, minor or certificate requirements, including prerequisites, without the program DUS permission. S requires work equivalent to C- or better; U gives no credit. This exception requires individual approval, not automatic eligibility.

requirements.title: Entrance credit is subject to department acceptance
requirements.summary: AP, IPC and prematriculation college credit may meet departmental major/minor requirements only to the extent permitted by that department. Prematriculation coursework must meet the published conditions, including B- or better and exclusion of work used for the high-school diploma; acceptance is not inferred for any listed AI course.

requirements.title: Incoming transfer approval and local coursework
requirements.summary: For students transferring into Duke, the academic unit must approve transfer courses toward the major/minor/certificate. At least half of each credential must be completed at Duke. This college/school-specific evaluation rule is separate from host-degree residency.

requirements.title: Post-matriculation transfer approval
requirements.summary: Individually arranged transfer courses require advance approval from the subject DUS and appropriate dean, followed by completion and final official transcript review. Limits are two such courses for Trinity students and four for Pratt students; academic-dismissal transfers are limited to two within those totals.

requirements.title: Study-away transfer limits and approval
requirements.summary: GEO-facilitated study away permits up to four credits per semester or eight per year, potentially two more for summer; combined study-away and individually arranged transfers cannot exceed ten courses. Pratt transfers may include at most two engineering courses. Relevant DUS approval, GEO arrangements and final transcript review are required; non-Duke summer programs require GEO approval.

requirements.title: Transfer grading and credit equivalence
requirements.summary: Post-matriculation transfer courses require C- or better; P/F or equivalent grades are ineligible. The Registrar determines credit equivalence; Duke course credits are not assumed equivalent to semester or quarter hours. Transfer grades do not enter the Duke record/GPA, and work beyond the transfer limit cannot replace an earlier transfer course.

requirements.title: Trinity S/U approvals and course eligibility
requirements.summary: For Trinity students, the program must permit S/U credit toward its requirements. A course must permit voluntary S/U; courses numbered 500 or higher additionally require instructor permission. Only one voluntary S/U course credit per semester or summer term may be requested, by the withdrawal deadline; the change cannot be reversed. This is not automatic permission for any AI course.

requirements.title: Trinity individually arranged transfer-course conditions
requirements.summary: In addition to department acceptance and prior Dean/DUS approval, individually arranged transfer courses cannot coincide with Duke enrollment, including online Duke courses. Community/junior college work after Duke matriculation is ineligible. Summer courses require at least four weeks and 17 class meetings. A course previously passed at Duke with D-/D/D+ cannot receive replacement transfer credit. Overseas institutional accreditation must be confirmed; third-party transcript arrangements are ineligible. These conditions apply to Trinity students and do not import its general-education curriculum into this credential.

requirements.title: Core substitution limits
requirements.summary: COMPSCI 201 cannot be substituted. COMPSCI 250D/ECE 250D may replace 210D for Trinity CS majors, while Pratt ECE students still require 250D; other Pratt students must consult their DUS. A 230 substitute cannot count elsewhere in the CS major. Alternatives other than 231D/232 need a prerequisite permission number because DukeHub does not recognize substitutions automatically.

requirements.title: Conditional options from the CS substitutions guide
requirements.summary: These are optional routes subject to DUS approval, subsequent record amendment, no course reuse and no online substitutions. Guide/current-program discrepancies remain unresolved; these observations do not override the concentration curriculum.

notes: This record describes the current requirements for first-year Fall 2026 matriculants. Earlier cohorts retain a separately linked prior curriculum that is not mapped here; this date is not a program launch date.
The page states both two of three electives must be COMPSCI and three COMPSCI electives; eligibility remains unresolved. The comprehensive elective list is student-only in Stellic.

Public topic offerings are named options, not guaranteed schedules. Cross-listings are one course record; distinct special topics retain separate identities. Historical course numbers are not counted again. ECE480 is excluded from the BS elective pool by the source.

The concentration is partial because of the inaccessible comprehensive pool and unresolved/partially mapped substitutions. The source states 15 major units and 34 BS units; this record does not cover the entire host-degree curriculum.
Individual course descriptions, prerequisites, credits and public syllabi remain unknown. Published group units are not assigned to each listed course.

Review 2026-10-11: public 2026–27 bulletin tabs establish general grading, transfer approval and local-coursework policies; Trinity operational policies are explicitly scoped to Trinity students. The academic unit retains approval authority. No individual course acceptance or graduation eligibility is inferred.
